slides.title: The auto Keyword
slides.prompt: Introduced in C++11, the 'auto' keyword automatically infers variable data type from its initializer.
slides.codeSnippet:
auto a = 5;       // Deducted as int
auto b = 3.14;    // Deducted as double
auto c = "Hi";    // Deducted as const char*

slides.title: Auto Declaration
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to let the compiler deduce the type.

slides.title: Auto Requirement
slides.prompt: What is mandatory when declaring a variable with 'auto'?
options: It must be initialized immediately at declaration
It must be declared inside a function
It must be an integer type
slides.correctAnswer: It must be initialized immediately at declaration

slides.title: Auto with Floating Point
slides.prompt: What type is inferred for 'auto x = 4.5f;'?

slides.title: Type Safety of auto
slides.prompt: Is 'auto' statically typed at compile time or dynamically typed at runtime?
options: Statically typed at compile time (type cannot change later)
slides.correctAnswer: Statically typed at compile time (type cannot change later)

slides.title: Auto Character Inference
slides.prompt: Fill in the inferred type for 'auto ch = 'Z';'.

slides.title: Changing Auto Variable Type
slides.prompt: If 'auto val = 10;', can you later do 'val = "Text";'?
options: No, type is fixed to int at compile time
slides.correctAnswer: No, type is fixed to int at compile time

slides.title: Auto Const Modifier
slides.prompt: Fill in the combined modifier for an unchangeable auto variable.

slides.title: Primary Benefit of auto
slides.prompt: What is a major advantage of using 'auto' in modern C++?
options: Simplifies complex iterator and template type declarations
slides.correctAnswer: Simplifies complex iterator and template type declarations

slides.title: Auto Expression Deduction
slides.prompt: What type is inferred for 'auto res = 5 + 2.5;'?
